subject: zoology
question_text: How do you justify the statement — "heart in fishes is a branchial heart"?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.55, VSAQ 112). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two chambers
steps.margin_note: State the number of chambers and name them. The venous heart line is a bonus.
lines: The heart of a fish is two chambered.
It has one auricle and one ventricle.
It holds only deoxygenated blood, so it is also
steps.why: A two chambered heart can hold only one kind of blood, and that single fact is what forces all of it to go to the gills first.
common_mistakes: Writing that the fish heart has three chambers. Three chambers appear first in amphibians.
Saying it carries oxygenated blood. The fish heart holds deoxygenated blood only.
steps.memory_tip: Two chambers, one kind of blood, one destination: the gills.

steps.label: Pumps to the gills
steps.margin_note: The justification is the mark here, not the name. Say where the blood is sent.

lines.text: Pumps blood straight to the gills: branchial

lines: The ventricle pumps this blood directly to the
gills, where it takes up oxygen.
Branchiae means gills. Because the heart sends
its blood to the gills and nowhere else first,
it is called a branchial heart.
steps.why: The name is justified by the destination of the blood, so the answer must trace where the blood goes before it names the heart.
common_mistakes: Naming the heart branchial without saying where the blood goes. The reason is the mark.
Writing that the heart pumps blood to the body first. The gills come first in a fish.
steps.memory_tip: Branchiae means gills, so a branchial heart is a heart that serves the gills.

insider_note: This is a justify question, so the words because it pumps blood directly to the gills must appear; simply naming the heart branchial scores nothing.
